item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
This is, while not the best tale I've ever read, surely flawless in its own right. The pacing is perfect and doesn't make me think "meh, bored, next" while also not overwhelming with details, the plot is very simple and easy to follow yet really good, the idea behind it is ambitious but pretty damn cool, it even has a plot twist that doesn't come out as forced in spite of its super short story, it doesn't even fall into the common clichés of using always the same O5 numbers (01 and 13) or assuming the Foundation's america only. Hell even the title is perfect, not giving away the main SCP (if it was "we need to talk about 055" it would have had a massively different effect) and the we need to talk really does give a bit of nervosism.

I see why it has the highest Upvote/Vote ration in the site.

I went through the list as well and couldn't find it, and I think there are five possibilities:

1. The MTF Xi-3 used to exist.
2. It never existed and the author misremembered a different MTF (I love irony.)
3. It exists but is concealed by an anti-meme, like you said.
4. It doesn't exist yet because the author invented it for the tale, but hasn't quite gotten around to writing descriptions and tales about the MTF.
5. MTF Xi-3 is SCP-055 (Not likely, I know, but it wouldn't be the first time the Foundation used skips as task-forces.)

item.title: Most positively rated article
item.content:encoded:
In celebration of this masterpiece hitting 500 soon, I thought I'd share something neat.

Thanks to the lovely sccper website, I've learned that this article is the most positively rated on the site in terms of upvote/downvote ratio. In fact, this article does not have a *single downvote* (knock on wood). Even Gears' Document Recovered From the Marianas Trench (which is the second most positively rated) has four downvotes.

In a collaborative writing project like this, creating a work of fiction that absolutely everyone enjoys with no dissenting opinions is an incredible accomplishment. Well done, qntm.

item.title: All of my yes
item.content:encoded:
Definitely +1'd, and still one of my favorite tales, although I'm a bit skeptical on a few things.

The SCP that follows Marion was clearly able to take Clay's gun without him noticing… But what about the O5? Perhaps it's taken to be assumed that it also robbed the memory of the theft from the O5, but I personally dislike making such assumptions.

This also means her "pet" works on other antimemes. Maybe not as weak as she makes it out to be after all.

Another thing I'm skeptical about is the actual receptionist - wouldn't she have mentioned something to the O5 about Clay? I'd imagine you'd have to be a cut above the rest of the receptionists to be working for an O5, so I'd expect her to be at least somewhat more perceptive… But again, assumptions and what not.

Regardless, I love her character. She's a strong independent woman who don't need no man.

item.content:encoded:
055 has always been about being defined in negative terms. Since you can be "not strong" but may also be "not weak" it shows, to *my* mind, that Marion can fall into the common trap many in the Foundation do - thinking they know more than they actually do.

Which she probably realizes she and it gives her a migraine when she thinks about too hard. Which she has to because it's her job.

But that's my head cannon.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I'm sorry folks but I'm sticking to my guns on this one. It just felt like the right choice of word to me, and still does. I think it indicates Marion and her team are starting to "metagame" the artifacts in their position, determining facts by systematically eliminating negatives and looking at the shape of the hole in their knowledge that's left behind. I think there's a distinction between the facts determinable by direct experimentation (it's not green, it's not silver) and the facts determinable by indirect meta-analysis of those various experiments.

I also think it's a more powerful statement to say outright that SCP-055 is "weak" rather than "not strong" because it lays down clearly that SCP-055 is at the bottom, not the top, of its particular hierarchy, which is a pretty alarming prospect. And, of course, that Marion is stronger.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
First off, I'm pretty sure this tale is an antimeme, because I cannot describe how incredible it is. Antimemes were very in-depth and perfectly described, without being described at all.
Just one thing:

SCP-055 is, as described in the file, a powerful information autosuppressor. As far as experimentation has uncovered, it can only be defined in negative terms. We can only record what it isn't. We know it isn't Safe or Euclid. We know it isn't round, or square, or green or silver. We know it isn't stupid. And we know it isn't alone. But what we do know is that it's weak. It's weak because it's the only antimemetic agent in our possession which has a physical entry in the files. We have paper records of the thing. We have containment procedures. It's not Safe, which means it's dangerous… but it's contained.

If it can only be described in the negative, the wording should be that it cannot be defined in positive terms. This minor detail is repeated a few more times, but nothing serious. Something interesting that I would love to hear about is how the thing reacts to double-negative descriptions. Other than that small bit of nitpicking, it's great.
